items.title: The longest German word in use
items.claim: German allows long noun compounds. A famous legal-administrative example abolished in 2013 was:
items.reveal:
The cattle-marking-and-beef-labelling-supervision-duties-delegation-law was repealed in 2013, partially because EU rules changed.

The Duden does not generally treat such legal compounds as 'words' for dictionary purposes.
items.why: Morphological possibility is not the same as everyday usage.

items.title: When the Grimms began publishing
items.claim: The first edition of the Brothers Grimm's Kinder- und Hausmarchen appeared in which year?
items.reveal:
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected tales partly from middle-class informants of Huguenot background, including Dorothea Viehmann.

Later editions softened violence in some tales. Their later Deutsches Worterbuch project was completed only in 1961.
items.why: The 'folk' in folklore is often more bourgeois and literate than the framing implies.

items.title: Luther's Bible and standard German
items.claim: Martin Luther's complete German Bible was published in which year, and which dialect did it draw on as a base?

options.text: 1534, drawing on the East Central German of the Saxon chancellery

items.reveal_title: 1534, based on chancellery East Central German
items.reveal:
Luther's New Testament appeared in 1522; the complete Bible in 1534. The work spread widely with printing and influenced the form of Standard German over the following centuries.

Mid-19th-century unification of orthography accelerated the standard's reach.
items.why: A widely read religious translation can shape a literary language for centuries.
